# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

#### Static Assertions (Compile-time Testing)

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {

    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`

```cmake
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
```

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp

// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly
```

description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`

content.text:
Implemented, built, and tested. The changes are uncommitted on jusprin-newui, and the rebuilt app is running now at the Home screen with the arrow headband project ready to open.

**What changed for the person.** In the project chat a turn is now one item: your message, one quiet line for the Agent's work, its reply, then the turn's changes as one block. While the turn runs the line reads the action in flight and the seconds since your message, ticking and shimmering, for example "Preview a printer setup… · 6s". When it ends the line reads "Worked for 44s · 17 actions" and opens into one plain line per action, edits in the primary text colour, lookups in secondary, a failed one in red with its message. Empty tool-only bubbles are gone. A printer setup's three preset switches read as one row, "Switched to Bambu Lab A1" with the process and filament in the meta, and three placements merge into one "3 steps merged" row. The printer panel is untouched.

**The mid-turn restore points had a different cause than I first said.** They did not come from the autosave probe. Before every mutating tool call the shell pinned a version, and after it saved again, so each agent edit cost two full project saves. Now the first edit of a model turn pins once, later edits in the same turn reuse that version, the turn's end saves the result through the existing chat checkpoint, and the autosave probe holds its model capture while a turn runs. Stop still works through the composer and still ends the turn with that one save. An edit from an external MCP client outside a turn behaves as before.

**Verified:**
- Page tests: 553 pass, including new tests for the turn line, the opened log, the ticking clock, the merged rows, and the printer panel staying as it was.
- Agent bridge tests: 381 pass, with a new check that messages reach the page stamped with their time.
- Token guard passes with the one new motion token.
- The production thread components render the saved "yes" chat as shown in the picture above.

**Not verified, and why.** The app's web view ignores background clicks, so I could not open the project in the running app from here. Two things need a real model turn, which the spend rule says I should not run without your go-ahead: the shimmering, ticking line during a turn, and that only one Revert appears per turn afterwards. Opening the arrow headband project in the app that is running now and sending any request that edits the plate would show both.

**Files to look at** if you want to review: [TurnActivity.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/TurnActivity.tsx) for the line, [MessageList.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx) for the turn grouping, and [ShellController.cpp:478](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:478) for the one-version-per-turn rule.

Web search results for query: "disclosure chevron convention collapsed chevron right expanded chevron down vs accordion chevron down up"

Links: [{"title":"esrf.fr","url":"https://gitlab.esrf.fr/icat/data-portal/-/merge_requests/415"},{"title":"expand down vector","url":"https://www.conceptdraw.com/examples/expand-down-vector"},{"title":"chevron down","url":"https://www.conceptdraw.com/examples/chevron-down"},{"title":"Progressive disclosure","url":"https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/progressive-disclosure"},{"title":"Tuesday, January 26, 2021","url":"https://mjtsai.com/blog/?p=31439"},{"title":"Progressive disclosure","url":"https://primer.style/ui-patterns/progressive-disclosure"},{"title":"disclosure triangle images right and down arrow","url":"https://www.conceptdraw.com/examples/disclosure-triangle-images-right-and-down-arrow"},{"title":"Progressive disclosure","url":"https://primer.style/design/ui-patterns/progressive-disclosure"},{"title":"mjtsai.com","url":"https://mjtsai.com/blog/wp-json/wp/v2/posts/31439"}]

The sources show two conventions, and they're used in different places.

- **State-based (right when collapsed, down when expanded):** An ESRF GitLab merge request says that when chevrons sit on the left of an accordion header, the common pattern is right-pointing when collapsed and down-pointing when expanded, citing MUI and Ant Design as examples. The chevrons are on the left-hand side in an accordion is the setup it describes. Apple's iOS and Mac style also uses this pattern. A right-pointing chevron (or triangle, depending on the OS) indicates the collapsed state, and a down-pointing chevron indicates the expanded state.
- **Down-when-collapsed, up-when-expanded:** The same GitLab thread says this version is more typically seen when the chevrons are on the right-hand side (cf. Bootstrap, Headless UI). Primer's guidance describes the same up/down alternation: it is typically positioned vertically, and alternates between the "up" state when expanded and the "down" state when collapsed.
- **Action-based (down means "open me"):** Some platforms show what a tap will do rather than the current state. In the Facebook/Android style, a down-pointing chevron is a button you tap to expand more content, and an up-pointing chevron is a button you tap to collapse it. Under this model, the same down chevron means different things on iOS and Android, which is the main source of confusion. The Mac/iOS style is described in the same source as a down-pointing chevron means "is open, tap to close".

The search also turned up Microsoft-derived guidance, through ConceptDraw's copies of Windows documentation, that a rotating triangle is preferred for hierarchical disclosure, and that custom arrow glyphs are best reserved for complex cases where a standard chevron can't communicate the control's behavior.

Takeaway: the "right collapsed, down expanded" pattern is the more common choice for left-side chevrons in accordions, while "down collapsed, up expanded" is more typical for right-side chevrons. Whichever you pick, keep the state-based or action-based model consistent across the product.

content.text:
Both changed, rebuilt, and the app is relaunched with the new page so you can see them live.

**The chevron.** You were half right, and the convention depends on where the chevron sits. A chevron at the far edge of a row points down when closed and up when open, which is what Bootstrap and GitHub's Primer do and what I had drawn. A chevron right after the words points right when closed and down when open, which is what ChatGPT, Claude and Apple's disclosure controls do. Since you read it the second way, the line now puts the chevron right after the words, pointing right while closed and down once open, as in the picture above.

**The running glyph.** Agreed, a still arrow says nothing. The glyph now rotates once a second while the turn runs, both on the line and on a running action inside the opened log, and it stops when the turn ends. The words next to it keep their shimmer. Readers who asked their system for reduced motion get a still glyph and plain words. The one-second period is a new token next to the shimmer one, guarded by the token test.

Verified: the page suite passes at 555 tests with two new ones for the glyph states, the token guard passes, and the rebuilt bundle inside the app carries the spinner. The rotation itself cannot show in a still picture, so that part is for you to see in the running app, which is open at Home with the arrow headband project ready.

Sources on the convention: [Primer, progressive disclosure](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/progressive-disclosure), [an ESRF discussion comparing MUI, Ant Design, Bootstrap and Headless UI](https://gitlab.esrf.fr/icat/data-portal/-/merge_requests/415), [Michael Tsai on the iOS and Android chevrons](https://mjtsai.com/blog/?p=31439).

# ChatToolActivity

The card under an Agent message that shows one action the Agent wants to take or is taking, from asking permission to the outcome.

- You supply `title` (what the action is: "Update print settings"), `status`, and `message` (one line for that status). For `pending` pass `onApprove` and `onReject`; for `running` pass `progress` (0 to 100, or leave it out when unknown) and `onCancel`.
- Statuses: `pending` waits for approval with Approve and Reject; `running` shows a `Progress` track and a Cancel link; `succeeded` and `failed` report the result; `cancelled` and `rejected` say that nothing changed.
- A `surface-subtle` card with a 1px `border-subtle` stroke, `radius-medium` corners and `space-12` padding, 300px wide. The title is `body-small-bold`; every status line is a 16px glyph plus `body-small` text, so status never rests on colour alone. Success uses `status-success` and failure `status-danger`.
- Write the message so it stands alone: "Applying changes · 60%", "Couldn't save changes. Please try again.", "Rejected. Your settings are unchanged."
- One card per action. A connection that needs a code composes a `FieldSecret` beside it rather than adding a variant.

</artifact-file-content>

<artifact-file-content>
JusPrin makes advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. It is a dense, native desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a chat Agent beside the 3D workspace. Build every surface to feel focused, assured, inventive and approachable.

## Voice and name

- Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Set it in the surrounding text colour; never put the gradient on small text.
- Be direct, capable and optimistic. Never cute, cryptic or over-engineered.
- Prefer plain language to slicer jargon. Say "Slice plate", not "Generate G-code".
- Make the next action obvious. One `ButtonPrimary` per view names the thing the screen is for; everything else is quieter.
- Buttons and labels are sentence case, verb first, with no full stop: "Add printer", "Open printer settings", "Undo".
- Address the person as "you". The Agent speaks as "I". No emoji anywhere in the product.
- A status is never colour alone: pair the colour with an icon and a plain-language label, such as a `circle-alert` glyph beside "Printer offline".

## Logo

- Use the files in `assets/Logos` as they are. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, recolour, outline, shadow or take the mark apart.
- Default to `jusprin-mark.svg` for application icons and small product contexts, and to the horizontal lockup when there is room for the name.
- Place the logo only on `neutral-white`, `neutral-mist`, `neutral-ink` or another quiet solid field, never over an image or pattern.
- Keep clear space of at least a quarter of the mark's width on every side.
- Minimum sizes on screen: 24px for the mark, 120px wide for the horizontal lockup. Below that, use the mark alone.
- Use the single-ink marks only when the gradient cannot be shown: `jusprin-mark-ink.svg` on light grounds, `jusprin-mark-white.svg` on dark ones.

## Colour

- Style product UI with the semantic tokens (`surface-*`, `text-*`, `border-*`, `action-*`, `status-*`). The primitives (`brand-*`, `neutral-*`) are the palette behind them, for brand artwork and covers, not a component API. The one exception is `Tooltip`, which is `neutral-ink` with `neutral-white` text in both modes.
- Page background is `surface-canvas`. Sidebars and grouped settings sit on `surface-subtle`. Dialogs, menus and popovers sit on `surface-raised` with an elevation shadow. A highlighted row inside them (hover or keyboard focus) is filled with `surface-raised-hover`, not `surface-subtle`, which would look sunk in on a dark menu.
- Body copy and values are `text-primary`; descriptions are `text-secondary`; metadata and placeholders are `text-tertiary`.
- `action-primary` is for the decisive action, the selected segment and text links. It is Orbit purple in light mode and Bloom pink in dark mode, so always put `action-on-primary` on it, never a literal white.
- Dark mode is a remapping of the same token names, not an inversion. Keep hierarchy, density and geometry identical and let the tokens change the values.
- The signature gradient runs from `brand-orbit` to `brand-bloom`. Reserve it for the logo, the splash screen, onboarding and rare hero moments. Never use it as ordinary product chrome.
- `axis-x`, `axis-y` and `axis-z` belong to the 3D viewport only. Never use them for status.
- A failed print or task is reported on `surface-failure-inverse`, a dark panel in both modes, with the `text-on-failure-*`, `status-danger-on-inverse` and `border-on-failure` tokens. Do not mix the ordinary text tokens onto it.

## Typography

- One family for all product UI: HarmonyOS Sans SC in Regular (400) and Bold (700), with the system UI font as fallback. There are no other weights and no italics.
- Use the ten type styles as they are and pick the nearest one; never set a bespoke size. `page-title` 24/30, `section` 18/24, `body` 14/20, `body-small` 13/18, `label` 12/16, `metadata` 10/14, each with a bold partner.
- Bold is for emphasis inside a run of the same size: the primary action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside its detail.
- `code` (12/16, the system monospace font) is only for code, keys, file paths, commands and IDs. Names, words, numbers and measurements stay in the sans face; its digits are already equal width, so changing values do not shift.
- Letter spacing is 0 everywhere. Capitals are reserved for short eyebrow captions set in `metadata-bold`, such as "CURRENT SETUP", "STEP 1 OF 3" and menu section titles; type them in capitals rather than transforming the text.

## Layout and geometry

- Whole-screen structure (top bar, panes, where menus open) is in the Application layout section. Every screen in the design file is on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), one page per page of the design file, and is specified layer by layer in the files under `screens/`.
- Design for a dense desktop application measured in device-independent pixels. Do not import web habits: no oversized controls, blur, glass or hero spacing inside the application shell.
- Space with the scale only: `space-4`, `space-8`, `space-12`, `space-16`, `space-20`, `space-24`, `space-32`, `space-40`, `space-48`.
- Controls take `radius-small` (4px). Containers such as cards, popovers and chat bubbles take `radius-medium` (8px), and so does `ButtonPrimary`, the one branded action. Sheets and large dialogs take `radius-large` (12px). Radii of 16px and above are for onboarding and marketing only.
- Borders are 1px `border-subtle`, drawn inside the box so a bordered control keeps its stated height.
- Control heights are compact: 26px for fields, selects and text links, 28px for chips and reply choices, 30px for a segmented control, 32px for a secondary or icon button, 34px for a primary or split button, 36px for a menu row.
- Shadows mark elevation, not decoration: `elevation-subtle` for tooltips, `elevation-medium` for menus and popovers, `elevation-strong` for sheets and dialogs. Flat surfaces carry no shadow.
- Every progress track is `component-progress-height` (4px) thick.

## Iconography

- Functional icons are Lucide 1.47.0 outlines, kept unchanged in `assets/Icons`. Inline the SVG and colour it with the surrounding text token through `currentColor`.
- Draw icons at 16, 20 or 24px. The only exception is the 14px fact glyph inside the setup card (`component-setupCard-iconSize`).
- Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom; do not approximate them with Lucide glyphs, and do not decorate with logo-derived shapes where a functional icon is clearer.
- No emoji and no filled icon sets.

## Components and states

- Every interactive component defines normal, hover, pressed, disabled and keyboard-focus states, plus success, warning and error where they apply.
- Hover and pressed change the fill, not the size: quiet controls go to `surface-subtle` then `surface-selected`; the primary action goes to `action-primary-hover` then `action-primary-pressed`.
- Fields show state on their stroke: 1px `border-subtle` at rest, `border-strong` on hover, 2px `border-focus` when focused, 1px `status-danger` with a message when wrong, and an `action-disabled` fill when disabled.
- Disabled controls keep their shape. Filled and icon buttons drop to 40% opacity, outlined buttons to 50%; fields, selects and chips switch to `action-disabled` and `action-disabled-text`. Do not hide a disabled action.
- Actions: `ButtonPrimary` once per view, `ButtonSecondary` for other labelled actions, `ButtonIcon` when a glyph alone is unmistakable, `ButtonLink` for low-emphasis moves such as "‹ Back" and "Undo", and `ButtonSplit` when the main action has alternatives.
- Entry: `FieldText`, `FieldSecret` for codes and keys, `FieldSearch` to filter a list, `FieldNumber` for one parameter, `FieldVerificationCode` for a six-digit code. Choice: `SegmentedControl` for two to five short options, `Select` for more, `Checkbox` for on or off, `Swatch` for a filament colour.
- Menus are a `MenuPopover` of `MenuRow`s, grouped with `MenuSectionTitle`. Focused tasks sit in a `Sheet`; an action that cannot be undone asks first with `DialogConfirmation`.
- Canvas tools use a `ToolPanel` of `FormRow`s. Status is shown with `StatusDot` and `Progress`, always beside words. `Stepper` marks position in a short setup sequence; `Tooltip` names icon-only controls; `DisclosureTechnicalDetails` folds away secondary detail.
- The Agent pane is built from `ChatHeader`, `PinnedSetupCard`, `ChatBubble`, `ChatReplyChoice`, `ChatAttachment`, `ChatToolActivity` and `Composer`. The header carries `ChipPrinterSpool`; the Home screen lists `ProjectCard`s and `PrinterCard`s.
- Draw every glyph with `Icon`.

## Accessibility

- Text meets 4.5:1 on the surface its token names; large text, control boundaries that carry meaning, icons and focus rings meet 3:1.
- Keyboard focus is a visible 2px `border-focus` ring, offset 2px. Never signal focus with a fill change alone.
- `status-warning` is the one exception in light mode, at about 2.5:1 on `surface-canvas`: use it for the warning glyph only, beside a `text-primary` label.
- `border-subtle` is decorative. A control must be recognisable by its label or glyph without it.

## Not synced

This design system and the JusPrin v2 canvas are the up-to-date JusPrin design. They began on 2026-10-13 as copies of a Figma file; since 2026-10-20 Figma is retired and out of date, and changes are made here directly. The font files cover Latin only; Chinese, Korean and Thai text falls back to the system font. `code` is the system monospace stack the application ships. Each component card shows its variants in light and in dark; where no dark variant is drawn, the dark panel is the light variant with the Dark values of the same tokens. Photographs and 3D renders appear as flat placeholders, and artwork larger than 64px is not drawn. The Agent cards and the components on the review page are on the canvas and in `screens/` but are not built as coded components.

</artifact-file-content>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds the JusPrin design-system files from the Figma export and the repo.

Usage: build_ds.py <repo root> <output dir>
Writes <output dir>/project/... ; uploads are done separately and their ids are

import json

import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(sys.argv[1])
OUT = Path(sys.argv[2]) / "project"
NOW = "2026-10-13T16:00:00Z"

def write(rel, text):
    p = OUT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- contrast
def lum(hexv):
    r, g, b = (int(hexv[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5))
    f = lambda c: c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
    return 0.2126 * f(r) + 0.7152 * f(g) + 0.0722 * f(b)


def ratio(a, b):
    la, lb = sorted((lum(a), lum(b)), reverse=True)

content.text:
Both fixed and published.

**The centred text.** WebKit centres the content of a button laid out as a flex row unless told otherwise, and the line is a button so it can open. Chrome does not, which is why my preview rendered left-aligned and the app did not. The rule now says left explicitly, the page is rebuilt, and the app is relaunched with it. Open the arrow headband project and the lines sit on the left like every other row.

**Design artifacts, now updated.**

- Design System (version 32): a new `ChatTurnActivity` component with its guideline, a card showing Working, Done closed and Done open in light and dark, the coded React component in the bundle and typings, the two motion tokens, and a line in the brand book's Agent pane list. The ChatToolActivity guideline now says the card is only for a running action with measured progress.
- JusPrin v2 canvas (version 40): a "Chat/Turn Activity · Light & Dark" review board beside Chat/System Line on the component review page, the turn line drawn into the five print-timeline boards under the two person turns that made the Agent work, with the live app's own wording "Worked for 9s · 3 actions", and the proposal board redrawn with the chevron after the words.

Links: [Design System](https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and [JusPrin v2 canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v).

One thing I found on the way that is worth knowing. The build sources for the design-system bundle in the figma-mirror folder were behind the live artifact. Someone had added the menu-row detail and the composer menus directly in the artifact, so regenerating from the sources would have thrown that work away. I patched the live files instead and brought the sources back in line with them. It is written up in memory so the next edit does not trip on it.

Draw an Agent turn's tool work as one line, and save one version per turn

One "yes" in the project chat produced seventeen Chat/Tool Activity
cards, each under an empty assistant bubble, with change rows between
them: three screens for one word. The cards were designed for the
approval flow, removed on 2026-10-07, and had no question left to ask.

message into one turn. Under the person's words sits one quiet line
(TurnActivity, the design system's new Chat/Turn Activity): while the turn
runs it names the action in flight and counts the seconds since the
message, the words shimmering and the glyph turning; done, it reads
"Worked for 44s · 17 actions" with a chevron right after the words, right
while closed and down once open, and opens into one line per action, edits
in text/primary, lookups in text/secondary, a failure in status/danger
with its message. Tool-only messages draw no bubble. The turn's changes

of a turn pins the version before it, later edits of the turn link to the
same one, the turn boundary's chat checkpoint saves the result, and the
autosave probe holds its model capture while the host is busy. One
version per turn, one Revert on its last row.
